newsitem.title: NORWAY: PLANS IN PLACE FOR NORTH SEA EKOFISK GAS BYPASS.
newsitem.headline: PLANS IN PLACE FOR NORTH SEA EKOFISK GAS BYPASS.

text.p: Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil) said on Thursday work on installing a 15.8-km Ekofisk bypass gasline is due to start on November 1 and continue until March 31.
Actual pipelaying to connect the existing Statepipe and Norpipe gas trunklines without passing through the Ekofisk centre is expected to take about 10 days.
Statoil said a special ferature of the project is that part of the Statpipe/Norpipe will be replaced with a completely new section, which will be welded into the working system.
The pressure of gas passing through the line will be reduced while work is underway.
Subsea welding will take place between April and May, actual tie-in of the new line will be in August.
The Ekofisk bypass is costed at 350 to 400 million.
